correctness.rationale: A length-m zero window is unique, rooting every cycle once; an Euler-circuit enumerator and exhaustive invertible-feedback enumeration yield identical canonical-cycle sets (2048 at m5). The arch-count characterization follows by constructing a shortest absent scattered subsequence; all 2^m cuts of each root and an independent next-occurrence DP are evaluated. Independent Python feedback/arch reimplementation reproduces (2,2):1, (3,4):2, m4 (5,7):8 and (6,7):8, and m5 (10,12):512,(11,13):1536. Independent orbit normalization reproduces the 528 reversal/complementation orbit classes and their 16/120/16/376 breakdown. The full saved CSV was not byte-recomputed; verify.py source and original Git blob were inspected. Finite proof only through m5.
residual_risks: Independent check is bounded to the stated finite ranges; any unrestricted proof rests on analyzed mathematics rather than numerical output.

value.rationale: The standard linearization of a de Bruijn cycle of order m has 2^m+m-1 letters to cover all m-factors once as a linear word. Its scattered-subsequence universality under all cuts is a separately motivated exact invariant; a complete census at first differing best-cut order is a useful finite boundary, even though the unpadded 512/1536 classification and symmetry orbits were known.
residual_risks: Overlapping earlier results substantially narrow novelty.
Does not prove an all-order padded formula.

final_claim: For binary de Bruijn cycles of order m=2..5, evaluating all cuts of the natural length-2^m+m-1 linearization gives exact (minimum,maximum) scattered-subsequence-universality pair distributions; at order five these are (10,12) for 512 cycles and (11,13) for 1536.
